summary: Orléans is a deck/bag-building worker placement game where you draw followers from a cloth bag and place them on a personal board to trigger actions, gradually upgrading your bag with better specialists. It's a tight, satisfying engine builder with light theme and a strong sense of steady improvement each round.
praised: Clean rules for the depth it offers
criticised: Can feel a bit solitaire with limited direct interaction
Trading/event track bookkeeping can slow turns

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with shared board spaces
interaction.detail: Players compete for limited slots on shared action spaces and the shared trade/travel tracks, so timing and first-mover advantage matter, but each player's engine (bag, board, followers) is entirely their own. There's no direct combat or resource theft.

subsystems: Farmland sets (endgame VP for distinct follower types collected)
scoring.how_you_win: Recruit followers and deploy them to advance along the development track, which scores points immediately, while also building trading posts and collecting sets of followers on farmland tiles for bonuses at game end when the round track runs out.
